q: Why is merge sort O(n log n)?
options: There are log n levels of halving and each level does O(n) merging
It sorts n/2 elements log n times
why: Halving n repeatedly takes log₂ n levels; all merges on one level together touch every element once.

q: When does quick sort hit O(n²)?
options: When the pivot is always the smallest or largest element
why: Then each partition only removes one element: n + (n − 1) + … = O(n²). A random pivot makes this extremely unlikely.

q: Extra space used by standard merge sort on an array?
why: Merging needs a temporary buffer for the merged output.

q: After one Lomuto partition, what is guaranteed?
options: The pivot is at its final sorted position, smaller values to its left
why: Everything left of the pivot is smaller and everything right is ≥ it, so the pivot never moves again.

q: You need the k-th largest element, not the whole sorted array. Which idea from this topic helps?
options: Quickselect: partition and recurse into only one side
why: Recursing into one side only gives n + n/2 + n/4 + … = O(n) average.

q: Merging [1, 4, 7] and [2, 3, 9] takes the fronts in which order?
why: Always take the smaller front element; when one list runs out, append the rest of the other.
